To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the growth of spruce sapling in old-growth forests is more dependent on canopy gap size than on the annual climatic variation.

( i) sapling growth was positively associated with gap size and, to a lesser extent, with the sapling's height and ( ii) the impact of annual climatic variability on the growth of Norway spruce saplings was greater in smaller gaps and under the intact canopy.
